question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=3x(t)+3 \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-x(t)+2y(t)-3\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of ODEs above. The equilibrium point of the system is $[-1,\,1]^{T}.$ Which of the following is the system obtained by shifting the equilibrium to the origin?
question.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get

$$
{x}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]x+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

where $x=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$

To shift the system's equilibrium from ${x}^{∗}$ to the origin, we define the deviation vector

$$
u=x-{x}^{∗},
$$

where $u=[\begin{aligned}u(t) \\ v(t)\end{aligned}].$

In our case, we have

$$
u=x-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,⇒\,x=u+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,\text{and}\,{x}^{′}={u}^{′}.
$$

Substituting $x$ and ${x}^{′}$ into the given system, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′} & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]x+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′} & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}](u+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}])+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]u+[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]u+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the shifted system is the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{u}^{′}(t)=3u(t) \\ {v}^{′}(t)=-u(t)+2v(t)\end{aligned}
$$
